name: ArgumentDescriptor.__init__
reason: Applies in substance: only type/range asserts that hold for the 24 static descriptors and four field stores, run at import; the stored fields reach genops through argReader, a name table the difftest checks. The prefix would be more exact as internal-bootstrap, since the stores are observable.

name: read_uint1
reason: readUintN 1 is `f.read(1)` plus the length test (`if data:` is the same as len == 1) and the exact message (:221-224); ReadUintExact pins the value struct.pack wrote at any position, and ValueError on short input, so a reader that pads, skips the check or always raises fails.

name: read_uint2
reason: readUintN 2 (:242-245); ReadUintExact pins the little-endian value for every n < 2**16 and ValueError on fewer than 2 bytes.

name: read_int4
reason: readInt4 mirrors :263-266, but ReadInt4Roundtrip states only the success path. The truncated-input ValueError (:266) is not stated, unlike in ReadUintExact and ReadFloat8Exact, so a read_int4 that pads or returns the short data passes.

name: read_uint4
reason: readUintN 4 (:284-287); ReadUintExact pins value and short-input ValueError.

name: read_uint8
reason: readUintN 8 (:305-308); ReadUintExact pins value and short-input ValueError.

name: read_stringnl
reason: readRawnl, stripQuotes and escapeDecode mirror :344-362 for the default arguments (the decode=False/stripquotes=False uses are inlined into the callers), but ReadStringnlPlain assumes `0x5c ∉ body`, which removes the docstring's own promise that embedded escapes are undone (:339-341). No theorem states the 'no newline found' ValueError (:345-346), the quote-mismatch or no-quote errors (:352-358), or what escape_decode does, so a read_stringnl that ignores escapes, skips the newline check or skips the closing-quote check passes. Probed on 3.15.2: the plain statement holds.

name: read_stringnl_noescape
reason: readStringnlNoescape is readRawnl, escapeDecode and a strict UTF-8 decode, as `read_stringnl(f, stripquotes=False, encoding='utf-8')`. NoescapeNoBackslash pins every backslash-free line (decoded, or UnicodeDecodeError), and the refutation of NoescapeVerbatim pins the backslash case. The bug record exists, and on 3.15.2 a line holding only a backslash gives ValueError('Trailing \\ in string'). A verbatim reader, or one that skips the UTF-8 check, fails.

name: read_stringnl_noescape_pair
reason: The model is two readStringnlNoescape calls joined by 0x20, as `"%s %s"` at :395; the second conjunct of NoescapeNoBackslash pins `u + ' ' + v` for two decodable lines, so dropping the space, swapping the order or reading one line fails.

name: read_string1
reason: readString1 mirrors :420-426, but ReadCountedRoundtrip quantifies only over streams that hold the whole payload; the 'expected %d bytes in a string1, but only %d remain' path (:425-426) is not stated, so a reader returning the short payload passes.

name: read_string4
reason: readString4 mirrors :453-460, but ReadString4Roundtrip assumes a count below 2**31. Neither the negative-count ValueError (:454-455) nor the truncated-payload ValueError that the docstring shows (:447-450, :459-460) is stated, so a reader that takes the count as unsigned, or returns short data, passes. Probed on 3.15.2: b'\xff\xff\xff\xff' gives 'string4 byte count < 0: -1'.

name: read_bytes1
reason: readBytes1 mirrors :483-489; ReadCountedRoundtrip states only full payloads, so the truncated ValueError (:488-489) is unpinned and a reader returning short data passes.

name: read_bytes4
reason: readBytes4 is readCounted after readUint4 (:515-523); only full payloads are stated, though the docstring shows the truncated error (:509-512), so a reader without the length check passes. Citation: readCounted cites `@3.14.7:515-516`, which is unchanged code now at :517-518.

name: read_bytes8
reason: readCounted mirrors the `n > sys.maxsize` check and the length check (:550-558), but ReadCountedRoundtrip assumes `b.length ≤ ssizeMaxN` and full payloads. Neither the 'bytes8 byte count > sys.maxsize' ValueError (reachable: a uint8 count can be 2**64-1, and 3.15.2 raises it) nor the truncated error in the docstring (:543-547) is stated, so dropping either check passes. Citation: `@3.14.7:550-551` is unchanged code now at :552-553.

name: read_bytearray8
reason: readCounted plus the bytearray tag (:585-593). As for read_bytes8, neither the maxsize ValueError (:587-588) nor the truncated error the docstring shows (:578-582) is stated. readCounted's comment cites only the bytes4/bytes8 lines (stale `@3.14.7:` marks, unchanged code), not :587-588.

name: read_unicodestringnl
reason: readUnicodestringnl mirrors :612-617; ReadUnicodeNl pins the result to decodeRUE of the line (the load_unicode twin) and the exact 'no newline found ... unicodestringnl' ValueError, so both branches are stated. Probed: 20000 random lines agree with pickle._Unpickler.load_unicode on 3.15.2.

name: read_unicodestring1
reason: readUnicodestring1 mirrors :649-655, but ReadUnicodeRoundtrip assumes a full, decodable payload; the truncated ValueError shown in the docstring (:642-646) is not stated, so a reader that decodes the short data passes.

name: read_unicodestring4
reason: readCounted plus decodeUtf8SP (:688-696). The truncated error in the docstring (:681-685) is not stated, and the maxsize branch is dead for a uint4 count. The comment cites `@3.14.7:` lines of bytes4/bytes8, not :690-691.

name: read_unicodestring8
reason: readCounted plus decodeUtf8SP (:729-737). Neither the reachable 'unicodestring8 byte count > sys.maxsize' ValueError (:731-732) nor the truncated error in the docstring (:722-726) is stated.

name: read_decimalnl_short
reason: readDecimalnlShort mirrors :764-772 (the b'00'/b'01' hack before int(s)); DecimalShortTwin pins agreement with load_int on every complete line, so dropping the bool hack or a different int parse fails (error class not pinned, SameOutcome); the missing-newline raise is read_stringnl's. Probed: 30000 random lines agree with pickle._Unpickler.load_int on 3.15.2.

name: read_decimalnl_long
reason: readDecimalnlLong mirrors :785-788 (`s[-1:] == b'L'` strip, int(s)); DecimalLongTwin pins equality with the separately modelled load_long, message included, on every complete line, so not stripping L fails. Probed: 30000 random lines identical on 3.15.2.

name: read_float8
reason: readFloat8 mirrors :847-850 with the value kept as its big-endian bits (an exact encoding of `_unpack('>d')` on IEEE boxes); ReadFloat8Exact pins those eight bytes at any position and the exact short-input message, so a byte-swapped or padding reader fails.

name: read_long1
reason: readLong1 mirrors :890-894, but ReadLongRoundtrip states only well-formed encodings; the 'not enough data in stream to read long1' path (:892-893) is not stated, so a reader decoding the short data passes.

name: read_long4
reason: readLong4 mirrors :922-928, but ReadLongRoundtrip assumes count < 2**31 and full data. The negative-count ValueError (:923-924), which the long4 descriptor promises ('requires the size to be >= 0', :936-937), and the truncated error (:926-927) are not stated, so an unsigned-count reader passes.

name: StackObject.__repr__
reason: The body is `return self.name` (:977), one field and no branch: a `trivial:` exclusion, not coverage. No Lean function mirrors it; the model represents each stack object by its name string, and DisStackRepr is `cases; rfl` on disEnd's message format, a statement about dis :2591-2592. Probed true: dis(b'NN.') gives 'stack not empty after STOP: [None]'.

name: StackObject.__init__
reason: Applies in substance: type asserts that hold for the static stack objects and three stores, run at import to build the table (names checked against ToolsTable on 3.15.2: equal, no two objects share a name). internal-bootstrap would be the more exact prefix.

name: OpcodeInfo.__init__
reason: Applies in substance: asserts and stores for the static opcodes list, built at import. Its result is ToolsTable.opTable, which I compared field by field with pickletools.opcodes on 3.15.2 (68 entries: code, name, arg, proto, stack names, first doc line all equal). internal-bootstrap would be the more exact prefix.

name: assure_pickle_consistency
reason: The stated reason is wrong: it is not a test helper and is not 'called by no code'. :2290 calls it at import and :2291 deletes it, and it raises ValueError (failing the import) if the opcode table and pickle.py disagree. Re-note it as internal-bootstrap: called once at import (:2290), deleted (:2291), raises nothing on 3.15.2's consistent tables.

name: _genops
reason: genopStep and genopsLoop mirror :2305-2326 (getpos, read(1), code2op lookup, the exhausted and unknown-opcode messages, reader, end position, the STOP break), and the opcode table is exact. But every theorem is vacuous on failure: GenopsFuelEnough, GenopsWellFormed (positions contiguous from 0, STOP last), DisFollowsGenops and OptimizeRawCopy all assume a successful parse or compare two runs, so a genopStep that always raises passes all four. Nothing states that genops accepts any stream, or what it raises on an exhausted or unknown opcode. Citation: genopStep cites `@3.14.7:2277-2295`, which is unchanged code now at :2305-2323.

name: genops
reason: `return _genops(pickle)` (:2351); same entries as _genops and the same gap (an always-raising parse satisfies them). GenopsWellFormed also fixes hasTell = true, so the documented `pos is None` case without tell (:2345-2349) is stated nowhere.

name: optimize
reason: optStep and optEmit mirror :2365-2417 (PUT/MEMOIZE/FRAME/GET/PROTO order, header at pos 0, newids renumbering, pickler.get(None), frameless large copies). But OptimizeRawCopy assumes no PUT, GET, MEMOIZE or FRAME and protocol < 4, which removes the function's whole purpose ('removing unused PUT opcodes', :2357) and the GET/PUT rewriting the brief names. That behaviour is the open pickle-optimize-sound. Probed true on 3.15.2: 19723 random raw-only streams copied exactly. Citations: OptSt/optStep `@3.14.7:2331-2359`/`:2337-2359` and OptOut/optEmit `@3.14.7:2371-2388`/`:2372-2388` are unchanged code, now at :2359-2387/:2365-2387 and :2399-2416/:2400-2416.

name: dis
reason: The model mirrors the 3.15.2 body with the theme off: markPhase :2491-2519, memoPhase :2521-2540, argText :2542-2557, annotateLine with max(visible_len, annocol) :2558-2566, stackPhase :2574-2584, disEnd :2586-2592. The citations are correct. But DisFollowsGenops only constrains runs that raise nothing, and the refuted DisNoIndexError is one input, so a dis that raises IndexError on every stream satisfies both. None of the docstring's sanity checks (:2448-2459) is stated: the pop count, 'memo key never stored', 'can't store markobject', 'no MARK exists'. Neither are the rendered lines. Dropping any check passes. The refutation itself is true on 3.15.2: dis(b'(\x85t.') gives IndexError('list index out of range'), and bugs/pickle-tools-dis-mark-indexerror.yaml exists.

name: _Example.__init__
reason: test-support applies: _Example is used only by the module's doctests (:2681-2720, `from pickletools import _Example`), and its body is one store.
